# dlm command reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/maintain_skills.py from the dlm binary. Do not edit. -->

Every command and its own flags. These global flags work on all of them:

#### Options

```
      --address string      listen address host:port (default "127.0.0.1:17171")
      --allow-remote        allow binding a non-loopback address (requires TLS)
      --cache-dir string    cache directory
      --config string       path to a YAML config file (env DLM_CONFIG)
      --config-dir string   configuration directory
      --data-dir string     data directory (database, state)
      --home string         place all dlm directories below this directory (portable mode)
      --log-dir string      log directory
      --log-format string   log format: json, text (default "json")
      --log-level string    log level: debug, info, warn, error (default "info")
      --log-stderr          also write logs to stderr
  -o, --output string       output format: table, json, yaml (default "table")
      --server string       API base URL (default: derived from --address)
      --tls-cert string     TLS certificate file
      --tls-key string      TLS private key file
      --token string        API bearer token (default: read from the daemon's token file)
```

## dlm auth

Who you are to the daemon, and API tokens

### dlm auth whoami

Show the token this client uses: its name and scope

```
dlm auth whoami [flags]
```


## dlm browser

Use the internal headless browser

#### Synopsis

Open pages in the daemon's internal headless browser to find what they download: media manifests, files and JS-made downloads. The browser starts on demand, with the stored cookies of the site.

```
dlm browser [flags]
```

### dlm browser download

Download a candidate found by `browser resolve`

#### Synopsis

Create a task for candidate INDEX of the resolve result RESULT_ID. Files the browser downloaded itself (blob and attachment downloads) are imported; other candidates are downloaded from their URL. HLS playlists (.m3u8) use the HLS engine; DASH manifests (.mpd) use the DASH engine.

```
dlm browser download RESULT_ID INDEX [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --dir string        absolute download directory
      --name string       file name (default: the one the page announced)
      --paused            create the task paused
      --priority string   priority: low, normal or high
      --queue string      queue ID or name (default: Main)
```

### dlm browser profiles

Manage browser profiles

#### Synopsis

Each site group has its own browser profile, which keeps the logins of the pages opened there.

```
dlm browser profiles [flags]
```

### dlm browser profiles list

List browser profiles

```
dlm browser profiles list [flags]
```

### dlm browser profiles rm

Delete a browser profile (its cookies and storage)

```
dlm browser profiles rm GROUP [flags]
```

### dlm browser resolve

Open a page in the headless browser and list its downloads

#### Synopsis

Open URL in the headless browser and list the downloads it led to (the candidates). The result is kept for a while: pass its ID and a candidate INDEX to `dlm browser download`.

```
dlm browser resolve URL [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm browser resolve https://example.com/watch?v=1
  dlm browser download 4f3a… 0 --queue Main
```

#### Options

```
      --wait int   seconds the page may keep producing downloads (default: the daemon's, 20)
```

### dlm browser status

Show the headless browser in use and the running browsers

```
dlm browser status [flags]
```


## dlm capture

Create a task from a captured browser download

#### Synopsis

Create a task the way the browser extension does: with the page, referrer, headers, user agent, cookies and media candidates the download was found with, which later let the link be refreshed.

Give the URL as an argument and describe the context with flags, or pass the extension's full JSON request with --request FILE ('-' reads stdin; cookies and media candidates can only be set this way). Flags override the file. The request's cookies are stored in the cookie store first, or kept for this download only with --cookie-scope task.

```
dlm capture [URL] [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm capture https://cdn.example.com/f.zip --page-url https://example.com/get --referrer https://example.com/
  dlm capture -r capture.json --paused
```

#### Options

```
      --allow-duplicate       add the task even when another task has the same link
      --checksum string       expected checksum ALGORITHM:HEX (md5, sha1, sha256 or blake3)
      --cookie-scope string   task (cookies kept for this download only) or store (the cookie store); default store
      --dir string            absolute download directory
      --filename string       file name chosen by the browser
      --final-url string      URL after redirects; this is what is downloaded
      --header stringArray    request header Name=Value to repeat (repeatable; Cookie and Host are ignored)
      --mime string           content type the browser saw
      --mirror stringArray    another link to the same file (repeatable)
      --name string           file name for the task (wins over --filename)
      --page-url string       web page the link was found on
      --paused                create the task paused
      --priority string       priority: low, normal or high
      --queue string          queue ID or name (default: Main)
      --referrer string       Referer to send (default: the page URL)
  -r, --request string        JSON capture request file ('-' for stdin)
      --resolver string       how to turn the link into a download: direct (default), ytdlp or browser
      --size string           size the browser saw: bytes, or a number with a unit: K/M/G (×1024), KB/MB/GB (×1000), KiB/MiB/GiB (×1024); 0 = unlimited
      --user-agent string     user agent the browser used
```


## dlm category

Manage the categories that sort downloads into directories

#### Synopsis

A category sends downloads to a directory by file extension or MIME type; the first matching category wins. They are used when the autoCategorize setting is on (dlm settings set autoCategorize=true) and the task has no directory of its own.

```
dlm category [flags]
```

### dlm category add

Create a category

```
dlm category add NAME [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm category add Videos --dir Videos --ext mp4 --ext mkv --mime 'video/*'
```

#### Options

```
      --dir string         directory of the downloads: absolute, or relative to the download directory (required)
      --ext stringArray    file extension without the dot (repeatable)
      --mime stringArray   MIME type or family such as video/* (repeatable)
```

### dlm category get

Show a category

```
dlm category get ID [flags]
```

### dlm category list

List categories in the order they are tried

```
dlm category list [flags]
```

### dlm category match

Show the category a file would be sorted into

```
dlm category match [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm category match --name movie.mkv
```

#### Options

```
      --mime string   MIME type
      --name string   file name
```

### dlm category rm

Delete a category (files already sorted by it stay where they are)

```
dlm category rm ID [flags]
```

### dlm category set

Change a category

#### Synopsis

Change the given fields of a category. --ext and --mime replace the whole list.

```
dlm category set ID [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --dir string         new directory
      --ext stringArray    new extension list (repeatable; replaces the old list)
      --mime stringArray   new MIME type list (repeatable; replaces the old list)
      --name string        new name
      --position int       new place in the order (0 is tried first)
```


## dlm config

Show or change the daemon's boot configuration

#### Synopsis

The boot configuration (listen address, logging, engines, ...) is read when the daemon starts. 'dlm config get' shows what the running daemon uses and where each value came from; 'dlm config set' writes the config file, and the change applies after 'dlm system restart'.

### dlm config get

Show the boot configuration (all of it, or one key or group)

```
dlm config get [KEY] [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm config get
  dlm config get log
  dlm config get server.address
```

### dlm config set

Change a key in the config file

#### Synopsis

Write KEY=VALUE into the daemon's config file after checking the result. Durations are written like 30s, lists comma-separated. --unset removes the key so its default applies again. The running daemon is not changed: restart it with 'dlm system restart'.

```
dlm config set KEY [VALUE] [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm config set log.level debug
  dlm config set server.fs_roots /data,/media
  dlm config set torrent.dht --unset
```

#### Options

```
      --unset   remove the key from the config file
```


## dlm cookies

Manage the cookie store

#### Synopsis

Manage the encrypted cookie store shared by the download engines.

Cookie values are never listed; `cookies export` writes them out on request.

```
dlm cookies [flags]
```

### dlm cookies clear

Delete every cookie of a domain

#### Synopsis

Delete every cookie stored for exactly DOMAIN (subdomains are separate domains).

```
dlm cookies clear --domain DOMAIN [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --domain string   domain whose cookies are deleted
```

### dlm cookies export

Export cookies (with their values) as JSON or Netscape cookies.txt

#### Synopsis

Write the unexpired cookies, values included, to stdout or --file (mode 0600). The default --output
table writes the bare file content; --output json|yaml prints the daemon's response instead.
The output contains secrets: keep it private.

```
dlm cookies export [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --domain string   only cookies of exactly this domain (no subdomains)
  -f, --file string     write to this file (mode 0600) instead of stdout
      --format string   file format: json, netscape (default "json")
      --name string     only cookies with this name
```

### dlm cookies import

Import cookies from a JSON or Netscape cookies.txt file

#### Synopsis

Import cookies from FILE ('-' reads stdin). The format (JSON array of cookies, such as a browser
extension's export, or Netscape cookies.txt) is detected unless --format is given. A cookie with the
same domain, name, path and partition key is replaced. Rejected cookies are reported on stderr.

```
dlm cookies import FILE [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --format string   file format: json, netscape (default: detect)
```

### dlm cookies list

List stored cookies (without values)

```
dlm cookies list [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --domain string   only cookies of exactly this domain (no subdomains)
      --name string     only cookies with this name
```

### dlm cookies rm

Delete a cookie

```
dlm cookies rm ID [flags]
```


## dlm credential

Manage stored site logins (HTTP Basic and Digest)

#### Synopsis

A stored login answers the Basic or Digest authentication challenge of downloads from its host. Passwords are stored encrypted and never shown. Basic credentials are sent in clear text over http:// links.

```
dlm credential [flags]
```

### dlm credential add

Store a login for a host

```
dlm credential add HOST [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm credential add files.example.com --user ann --password-stdin
  dlm credential add '*.example.org' --user bob --password s3cret --scheme digest
```

#### Options

```
      --password string   password (visible in the process list: prefer --password-stdin)
      --password-stdin    read the password from the first line of stdin
      --scheme string     auto (default), basic or digest
      --user string       user name (required)
```

### dlm credential get

Show a stored login (without its password)

```
dlm credential get ID [flags]
```

### dlm credential list

List stored logins

```
dlm credential list [flags]
```

### dlm credential rm

Delete a stored login

```
dlm credential rm ID [flags]
```

### dlm credential set

Change a stored login

```
dlm credential set ID [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --host string       new host
      --password string   new password (prefer --password-stdin)
      --password-stdin    read the new password from the first line of stdin
      --scheme string     new scheme: auto, basic or digest
      --user string       new user name
```


## dlm fs

Browse the daemon's machine (limited to server.fs_roots)

### dlm fs browse

List the directories below a path

#### Synopsis

List the sub-directories of a directory below server.fs_roots on the machine the daemon runs on, for choosing a download directory there. Without a path it lists the roots.

```
dlm fs browse [PATH] [flags]
```

### dlm fs free

Show the free space of a directory

```
dlm fs free PATH [flags]
```


## dlm health

Check that the daemon is running

#### Synopsis

Report the daemon's status and version and whether the API token is accepted.

Exits with an error if the daemon is unreachable or rejects the token.

```
dlm health [flags]
```


## dlm limits

Show the speed limits and quotas in force

#### Synopsis

Show the global and per-queue speed limits now in force, the active speed profile, the quota usage and a temporary override. 'dlm limits override' changes the global limit for a while.

```
dlm limits [flags]
```

### dlm limits override

Replace the global speed limit for a while

#### Synopsis

Replace the global speed limit by SPEED per second (500K, 2MB, ...; none or 0: unlimited, "turbo") for --minutes (1-1440, default 60). The configured limit and profiles apply again afterwards. --clear ends an override now.

```
dlm limits override [SPEED] [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm limits override           # turbo for an hour
  dlm limits override 1MB -m 30
  dlm limits override --clear
```

#### Options

```
      --clear         end the override now
  -m, --minutes int   how long the override lasts, 1-1440 (default 60)
```


## dlm logs

Show the daemon's log

#### Synopsis

Show the most recent records of the daemon's log (it keeps the last 5000 since it started; older ones are in its log directory). -f keeps printing new records. Table output prints one line per record; json prints one JSON object per line.

```
dlm logs [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm logs -n 50 --level warn
  dlm logs -f --q scheduler
  dlm logs --since 15m
```

#### Options

```
  -f, --follow         keep printing new records
      --level string   only this level and above: debug, info, warn or error
  -n, --lines int      how many of the newest records to show, 1-1000 (default 100)
      --q string       only records containing this text
      --since string   only records since this long ago (15m, 2h) or this time (RFC 3339)
      --until string   only records until this time (RFC 3339)
```


## dlm native-host

Native Messaging host for the browser extension

#### Synopsis

Run the Native Messaging host. Browsers start it (through the launcher that `native-host install` writes) when the extension calls runtime.connectNative; it answers `connect` with where the daemon is, and `pair` / `pair.status` so the extension can be given a token of its own, over stdin/stdout. It is not meant to be run by hand.

Without a subcommand it serves the protocol until stdin closes. Browser-supplied arguments (the caller's origin, --parent-window) are accepted.

```
dlm native-host [ORIGIN] [flags]
```

### dlm native-host install

Register the Native Messaging host with the browsers

#### Synopsis

Write the host launcher and register it, for the current user, with Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave and Firefox (manifest files on Linux and macOS, registry keys on Windows).

The published DLM extension (Chrome and every Chromium browser, and Firefox) is always registered; --extension-id and --firefox-id (or the chrome-extension:// entries of server.allowed_origins) add others, for example a build you made yourself. Another extension also has to be in server.allowed_origins to be answered.

```
dlm native-host install [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm native-host install
  dlm native-host install --extension-id abcdefghijklmnopabcdefghijklmnop --browser chrome
```

#### Options

```
      --browser stringArray        limit to these browsers: chrome, chromium, edge, brave, firefox (repeatable; default: all)
      --extension-id stringArray   Chromium extension ID or chrome-extension://ID/ origin to allow (repeatable; default: the chrome-extension:// entries of server.allowed_origins)
      --firefox-id stringArray     Firefox add-on ID to allow, e.g. dlm@example.org (repeatable)
```

### dlm native-host status

Show where the Native Messaging host is registered

#### Synopsis

Ask the daemon (it must run on this machine) whether the host is registered with each browser, for the user the daemon runs as.

```
dlm native-host status [flags]
```

### dlm native-host uninstall

Remove the Native Messaging host registrations

#### Synopsis

Remove the host registration from the selected browsers (default: all) and, when all were selected, the launcher.

```
dlm native-host uninstall [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --browser stringArray   limit to these browsers: chrome, chromium, edge, brave, firefox (repeatable; default: all)
```


## dlm openapi

Print the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the REST API

#### Synopsis

Print the OpenAPI document of the daemon's REST API, as the daemon serves it at /openapi.json, without starting a daemon or contacting one. JSON by default; -o yaml prints YAML. Releases publish it as a versioned artifact, which client generators (Dart, TypeScript, ...) read. --oas 3.0 prints the OpenAPI 3.0.3 downgrade (served at /openapi-3.0.json) for generators that do not understand 3.1.

```
dlm openapi [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm openapi > openapi.json
  dlm openapi -o yaml
  dlm openapi --oas 3.0 > openapi-3.0.json
```

#### Options

```
      --oas string   OpenAPI version to print: 3.1 or 3.0 (the 3.0.3 downgrade) (default "3.1")
```


## dlm pairing

Allow or refuse browser extensions that ask to connect

#### Synopsis

A browser extension asks to be paired and waits for you to allow it. The request shows a six-digit code that the extension shows too; allow it only when they match. Allowing issues the extension a token of its own (scope extension), which `dlm auth token list` shows and `dlm auth token rm` revokes.

### dlm pairing approve

Allow a pairing

```
dlm pairing approve ID [flags]
```

### dlm pairing deny

Refuse a pairing

```
dlm pairing deny ID [flags]
```

### dlm pairing list

List the pairings waiting for an answer

```
dlm pairing list [flags]
```

### dlm pairing show

Show a pairing (an approved one also prints its token, once)

```
dlm pairing show ID [flags]
```

### dlm pairing start

Ask to pair (what the extension's native host does)

```
dlm pairing start [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --browser string          chrome, chromium, edge, brave, opera, vivaldi, firefox or other
      --client-id string        the extension's id
      --client-version string   the extension's version
      --name string             what the client calls itself
```


## dlm plugin

Manage JavaScript plugins

#### Synopsis

Plugins are JavaScript extensions that resolve links the built-in engines cannot, refresh expired links, and react to downloads starting, failing and completing. A plugin runs inside the daemon and may contact the hosts its manifest lists (shown by dlm plugin get): install only plugins you trust.

```
dlm plugin [flags]
```

### dlm plugin disable

Switch a plugin off

```
dlm plugin disable NAME [flags]
```

### dlm plugin enable

Switch a plugin on

```
dlm plugin enable NAME [flags]
```

### dlm plugin get

Show a plugin

```
dlm plugin get NAME [flags]
```

### dlm plugin install

Install a plugin from a directory or a git repository

#### Synopsis

SOURCE is a directory holding manifest.json and the plugin's script, or an https:// git URL (the daemon needs git on its PATH). The manifest and script are checked and the script is run once before the plugin is kept. --replace upgrades an installed plugin of the same name.

```
dlm plugin install SOURCE [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm plugin install ./my-plugin
  dlm plugin install https://github.com/example/dlm-plugin.git --ref v1.2.0
```

#### Options

```
      --disabled     install the plugin switched off
      --ref string   branch or tag of a git source
      --replace      upgrade an installed plugin of the same name
```

### dlm plugin list

List installed plugins

```
dlm plugin list [flags]
```

### dlm plugin logs

Show a plugin's log

#### Synopsis

Show the latest log records of a plugin (500 are kept): what its script wrote with dlm.log and what the daemon said about it, such as failed starts and hooks.

```
dlm plugin logs NAME [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --level string   only this level and above: debug, info, warn or error
  -n, --lines int      how many of the newest records to show, 1-500 (default 100)
      --q string       only records containing this text
```

### dlm plugin rm

Uninstall a plugin and delete its files and stored data

```
dlm plugin rm NAME [flags]
```


## dlm queue

Manage download queues

```
dlm queue [flags]
```

### dlm queue add

Create a queue

```
dlm queue add NAME [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm queue add fast --max-concurrent 2 --speed-limit 1MB
```

#### Options

```
      --max-concurrent int   tasks the queue runs at once (setting maxConcurrentDownloads)
      --set stringArray      queue setting path=value (repeatable; value parsed as JSON when valid)
      --speed-limit string   queue speed limit in bytes/s: bytes, or a number with a unit: K/M/G (×1024), KB/MB/GB (×1000), KiB/MiB/GiB (×1024); 0 = unlimited
      --stopped              create the queue stopped
```

### dlm queue get

Show a queue

```
dlm queue get ID [flags]
```

### dlm queue list

List queues

```
dlm queue list [flags]
```

### dlm queue reorder

Move a queue to a 0-based position in the queue order

```
dlm queue reorder ID POSITION [flags]
```

### dlm queue replace-settings

Replace a queue's settings overrides with a JSON or YAML file

#### Synopsis

Replace all settings overrides of a queue with the settings object in FILE (JSON or YAML; '-' reads stdin).

```
dlm queue replace-settings ID -f FILE [flags]
```

#### Options

```
  -f, --file string   settings file (JSON or YAML; '-' for stdin)
```

### dlm queue rm

Delete a queue

#### Synopsis

Delete a queue. A queue that still has tasks needs --move-tasks-to; the Main queue cannot be deleted.

```
dlm queue rm ID [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --move-tasks-to string   queue ID that receives the deleted queue's tasks
```

### dlm queue set

Rename a queue or change its settings overrides

#### Synopsis

Rename a queue and/or patch its settings overrides. --set path=value and --unset path build a JSON merge patch (dotted paths, values parsed as JSON when valid); --unset makes the setting inherit again.

```
dlm queue set ID [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm queue set <id> --name fast --max-concurrent 3 --unset speedLimit
```

#### Options

```
      --max-concurrent int   tasks the queue runs at once (setting maxConcurrentDownloads)
      --name string          new queue name
      --set stringArray      queue setting path=value (repeatable; value parsed as JSON when valid)
      --speed-limit string   queue speed limit in bytes/s: bytes, or a number with a unit: K/M/G (×1024), KB/MB/GB (×1000), KiB/MiB/GiB (×1024); 0 = unlimited
      --unset stringArray    remove a queue setting override (repeatable)
```

### dlm queue settings

Show a queue's effective settings and where each value comes from

```
dlm queue settings ID [flags]
```

### dlm queue start

Start a queue (its tasks may run)

```
dlm queue start ID [flags]
```

### dlm queue stop

Stop a queue (running tasks return to queued)

```
dlm queue stop ID [flags]
```


## dlm resolve

Probe a URL without downloading it

#### Synopsis

Probe a URL with the effective settings and show what would be downloaded. The resolve ID can be passed to the API's create-task until it expires.

```
dlm resolve URL [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --queue string      queue ID whose settings apply (default: Main)
      --set stringArray   task setting override path=value (repeatable), e.g. retry.maxAttempts=3
```


## dlm resolve-many

Probe several URLs without downloading them

#### Synopsis

Probe up to 100 URLs, a few at a time, and show for each what would be downloaded, or why it failed, and whether another task already has it. The resolve IDs can be passed to the API's create-task until they expire.

```
dlm resolve-many URL... [flags]
```


## dlm serve

Run the dlm daemon

#### Synopsis

Run the dlm daemon in the foreground until interrupted.

On first start a random API token is written to the token file in the config directory (see `dlm token show`).

With --address 127.0.0.1:0 the system picks a free port; the daemon publishes it in runtime.json in the config directory, which the other commands read to find it. Only one daemon runs per config directory.

```
dlm serve [flags]
```


## dlm service

Start the daemon when you log in

#### Synopsis

Install or remove a login item for the current user that runs `dlm serve`: a launchd agent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux and a Run registry value on Windows. It does not need administrator rights.

### dlm service install

Start the daemon at login, and now

#### Synopsis

Install the login item and start the daemon through it now. It runs this `dlm` binary with `serve`, and with --home when this command was given one, so a portable setup stays portable.

```
dlm service install [flags]
```

### dlm service status

Show whether the daemon starts at login

```
dlm service status [flags]
```

### dlm service uninstall

Stop starting the daemon at login

#### Synopsis

Remove the login item and stop the daemon it started. A daemon you started yourself is not touched.

```
dlm service uninstall [flags]
```


## dlm settings

Manage the global settings

#### Synopsis

Manage the global settings layer. Values not set globally inherit the built-in defaults (`dlm settings defaults`); queues and tasks may override them.

```
dlm settings [flags]
```

### dlm settings defaults

Show the built-in default settings

```
dlm settings defaults [flags]
```

### dlm settings get

Show the global settings layer

```
dlm settings get [flags]
```

### dlm settings replace

Replace the global settings with a JSON or YAML file

#### Synopsis

Replace the whole global settings layer with the settings object in FILE (JSON or YAML; '-' reads stdin).

```
dlm settings replace -f FILE [flags]
```

#### Options

```
  -f, --file string   settings file (JSON or YAML; '-' for stdin)
```

### dlm settings schema

Describe the settings fields (type, group, bounds, levels)

```
dlm settings schema [flags]
```

### dlm settings set

Set global settings

#### Synopsis

Set global settings by dotted path. Values are parsed as JSON when valid (numbers, booleans, objects, arrays, quoted strings), else taken as a string.

```
dlm settings set PATH=VALUE... [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm settings set maxConnections=8 retry.maxAttempts=10 downloadDir=/data/downloads
```

### dlm settings unset

Unset global settings (they inherit the defaults again)

#### Synopsis

Unset global settings by dotted path; they inherit the built-in defaults again.

```
dlm settings unset PATH... [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm settings unset maxConnections retry.maxAttempts
```


## dlm stats

Show download statistics

#### Synopsis

Shows the number of tasks per status and per engine (protocol), the bytes downloaded, and what completed in the last 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days.

```
dlm stats [flags]
```

### dlm stats timeline

Show the traffic per hour or day

#### Synopsis

Show the bytes downloaded and uploaded per hour or day (UTC), optionally split by engine or queue. Defaults to the last 24 hours (--bucket hour) or 30 days (--bucket day).

```
dlm stats timeline [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm stats timeline
  dlm stats timeline --bucket day --group-by engine
```

#### Options

```
      --bucket string     hour (default) or day
      --from string       start of the range, RFC 3339 (inclusive)
      --group-by string   none (default), engine or queue
      --to string         end of the range, RFC 3339 (exclusive)
```


## dlm system

Inspect and control the running daemon

```
dlm system [flags]
```

### dlm system info

Describe the daemon: version, directories, engines, tools

#### Synopsis

Report the daemon's version, API version, build, process, listen address, directories, enabled engines, the status of the external tools (ffmpeg, yt-dlp, browser) and the database size.

```
dlm system info [flags]
```

### dlm system restart

Restart the daemon

#### Synopsis

Stop the daemon gracefully and start it again with the same arguments.

```
dlm system restart [flags]
```

### dlm system stop

Stop the daemon gracefully

#### Synopsis

Stop the daemon gracefully: running downloads are stopped and requeued, then it exits.

```
dlm system stop [flags]
```


## dlm task

Manage download tasks

```
dlm task [flags]
```

### dlm task add

Add download tasks

#### Synopsis

Add one task per URL (and per line of --file; '-' reads stdin, blank lines and # comments are skipped).

One URL creates a single task (create-task); several URLs or a file create them in one batch (create-tasks) and print one result per URL. Settings flags apply to every task.

A URL can be a magnet link, an ed2k:// link, or the path of a local .torrent file, which is sent to the daemon (files above 512 KiB are uploaded as they are).

--ytdlp downloads a video or audio page with yt-dlp instead of fetching the URL itself; --format picks the yt-dlp format (for example 'bv*[height<=720]+ba/b') or the quality of an HLS/DASH stream (for example 720).

```
dlm task add URL... [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm task add https://example.com/file.iso --queue <id> --speed-limit 1MB
  dlm task add -f urls.txt --paused
  dlm task add 'https://example.com/img[001-100].jpg' --expand
  dlm task add https://a.example/f.iso --mirror https://b.example/f.iso --mirror https://c.example/f.iso
  dlm task add ./ubuntu.iso.torrent 'magnet:?xt=urn:btih:...'
  dlm task add https://example.com/file.iso --checksum sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
  dlm task add --ytdlp 'https://video.example/watch?v=abc' --format 'bv*[height<=720]+ba/b'
  dlm task add https://example.com/a.bin --header 'Cookie=x=1' --set retry.maxAttempts=10
```

#### Options

```
      --allow-duplicate      add the tasks even when another task has the same link, checksum, or file name and size
      --checksum string      expected checksum ALGORITHM:HEX (md5, sha1, sha256 or blake3); a file that does not match is downloaded again
      --connections int      maximum connections per task (setting maxConnections)
      --dir string           absolute download directory (default: the effective downloadDir)
      --expand               expand ranges in the URLs: file[001-100].jpg is 100 tasks ([a-e] and [1-10:2] work too)
  -f, --file string          read URLs from this file, one per line ('-' for stdin)
      --format string        media format: a yt-dlp format selector with --ytdlp, or the quality of an HLS/DASH stream
      --header stringArray   extra request header Name=Value (repeatable)
      --mirror stringArray   another http(s) link to the same file (repeatable, single URL only)
      --name string          file name (single URL only; default: detected)
      --paused               add the tasks paused
      --priority string      priority: low, normal or high
      --queue string         queue ID (default: Main)
      --set stringArray      task setting path=value (repeatable; value parsed as JSON when valid), e.g. retry.maxAttempts=3
      --speed-limit string   speed limit per task in bytes/s: bytes, or a number with a unit: K/M/G (×1024), KB/MB/GB (×1000), KiB/MiB/GiB (×1024); 0 = unlimited
      --ytdlp                download the URLs with yt-dlp (video and audio pages)
```

### dlm task await-link

Wait for the browser extension to capture a new link

#### Synopsis

Put a failed or awaiting_link task into the awaiting_link state: the next download the browser extension captures that matches the task's size or file name becomes its new link. The wait ends after refresh.awaitTimeout.

```
dlm task await-link ID [flags]
```

### dlm task cleanup

Remove old completed downloads

#### Synopsis

Remove the completed tasks that finished at least --older-than days ago from the list, or every completed task with --all. --files also deletes their downloaded files. --dry-run only shows what would go. The retentionDays setting does this automatically (without touching files).

```
dlm task cleanup [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm task cleanup --older-than 30 --dry-run
  dlm task cleanup --all --files
```

#### Options

```
      --all              remove every completed task
      --dry-run          only show what would be removed
      --files            also delete the downloaded files
      --older-than int   remove tasks that completed at least this many days ago
      --queue string     only tasks of this queue ID
```

### dlm task expand

Show the URLs a pattern with ranges stands for

#### Synopsis

Show how many URLs a pattern such as 'https://example.com/img[001-100].jpg' stands for and list the first ones, before adding them with 'dlm add --expand'.

```
dlm task expand PATTERN [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm task expand 'https://example.com/img[001-100].jpg' --preview 5
```

#### Options

```
      --preview int   how many URLs to list, 0-1000 (default 20)
```

### dlm task export

Write tasks as a list (JSON, URL list or aria2 input file)

#### Synopsis

Writes the matching tasks to stdout, or to --file, as dlm JSON (default), one URL per line, or an aria2 input file. Only the link, mirrors, file name, directory, referrer and user agent are exported: captured headers and cookies, which may hold logins, never are. dlm task import reads the list back.

```
dlm task export [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm task export --format urls --status completed
  dlm task export -f backup.json
```

#### Options

```
  -f, --file string      write to this file instead of stdout (the format follows .json/.aria2/.txt)
      --format string    json (default), urls or aria2
      --queue string     only tasks of this queue ID
      --search string    only tasks whose name or URL contains this text
      --status strings   only tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
```

### dlm task files

List a task's files or choose which are downloaded

#### Synopsis

Without --select, list the files of a multi-file task (a torrent) and whether each is selected. With --select INDEX[,INDEX…] download only those files from now on (every other file is skipped). The task must be paused or not started: active and completed tasks cannot change.

```
dlm task files ID [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm task files 01J…
  dlm task files 01J… --select 0,3
```

#### Options

```
      --select ints   indexes of the files to download
```

### dlm task get

Show a task

```
dlm task get ID [flags]
```

### dlm task import

Add the downloads of a list (JSON, URL list or aria2 input file)

#### Synopsis

Reads a list written by dlm task export, a file of URLs, or an aria2 input file ('-' reads stdin) and adds one task per entry; entries that fail do not stop the others. The format follows the file extension (.json, .aria2, .txt) unless --format says otherwise.

```
dlm task import FILE [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm task import backup.json
  dlm task import downloads.aria2 --paused
  dlm task import - --format urls < urls.txt
```

#### Options

```
      --allow-duplicate   add tasks even when another task has the same link, checksum, or file name and size
      --dry-run           create nothing; show per entry whether it would be added or why not
      --expand            expand ranges in the URLs: file[001-100].jpg is 100 tasks
      --format string     json, urls or aria2 (default: from the file extension)
      --paused            add the tasks paused
      --queue string      queue ID (default: Main)
```

### dlm task list

List tasks

#### Synopsis

List tasks, one page at a time (--limit, --cursor) or all of them (--all follows the cursors).

The table shows the last 8 characters of each task ID; use -o json for full IDs.

```
dlm task list [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --all                       follow cursors and list every matching task
      --category string           only tasks of this category (ID or name)
      --completed-after string    only tasks completed at or after this time (RFC 3339)
      --completed-before string   only tasks completed at or before this time (RFC 3339)
      --created-after string      only tasks created at or after this time (RFC 3339)
      --created-before string     only tasks created at or before this time (RFC 3339)
      --cursor string             continue after this cursor (from a previous page)
      --engine string             only tasks of this engine (http, bt, ...)
      --label string              only tasks with this label: KEY or KEY=VALUE
      --limit int                 page size, 1-500 (default 50)
      --max-size value            only tasks of at most this size (500K, 2MB, ...)
      --min-size value            only tasks of at least this size (500K, 2MB, ...)
      --order string              direction: asc or desc (default: the one of --sort)
      --queue string              only tasks of this queue ID
      --search string             only tasks whose name or URL contains this text
      --sort string               sort: position (queue order, default), created (newest first), name, size or completed
      --status strings            only tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --total                     also count every matching task
```

### dlm task move

Move a task to the end of another queue

```
dlm task move ID QUEUE [flags]
```

### dlm task move-tasks

Move several tasks to another queue

#### Synopsis

Append each chosen task at the end of the queue given with --to. Chooses tasks by ID, or every task matching --all, --queue and/or --status. Prints one result per task; exits 1 if any failed.

```
dlm task move-tasks [ID...] [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --all              act on every task
      --queue string     act on the tasks of this queue ID
      --status strings   act on the tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --to string        target queue ID (required)
```

### dlm task pause

Pause tasks

#### Synopsis

Pause tasks by ID, or every task matching --all, --queue and/or --status. Prints one result per task; exits 1 if any failed.

```
dlm task pause [ID...] [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --all              pause every task
      --queue string     pause the tasks of this queue ID
      --status strings   pause the tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
```

### dlm task refresh

Get a new link for a task whose link expired

#### Synopsis

Run the task's refresh strategies (setting refresh.strategies) now. A refreshed task is queued again and resumes from where it stopped; when only waiting strategies remain the task waits in awaiting_link. Running tasks must be paused first.

```
dlm task refresh ID [flags]
```

### dlm task refresh-history

Show a task's link refresh history

```
dlm task refresh-history ID [flags]
```

### dlm task refresh-tasks

Refresh the links of several tasks

#### Synopsis

Run the refresh strategies of each chosen task now (see 'dlm task refresh'). Chooses tasks by ID, or every task matching --all, --queue and/or --status. Prints one result per task; exits 1 if any failed.

```
dlm task refresh-tasks [ID...] [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --all              act on every task
      --queue string     act on the tasks of this queue ID
      --status strings   act on the tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
```

### dlm task reorder

Move a task to a 0-based position within its queue

```
dlm task reorder ID POSITION [flags]
```

### dlm task restart

Download a completed or failed task again from scratch

```
dlm task restart ID [flags]
```

### dlm task restart-tasks

Download several finished or failed tasks again

#### Synopsis

Restart each chosen task from scratch. Chooses tasks by ID, or every task matching --all, --queue and/or --status. Prints one result per task; exits 1 if any failed.

```
dlm task restart-tasks [ID...] [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --all              act on every task
      --queue string     act on the tasks of this queue ID
      --status strings   act on the tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
```

### dlm task resume

Resume paused or failed tasks

#### Synopsis

Resume paused or failed tasks by ID, or every task matching --all, --queue and/or --status. Prints one result per task; exits 1 if any failed.

```
dlm task resume [ID...] [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --all              resume every task
      --queue string     resume the tasks of this queue ID
      --status strings   resume the tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
```

### dlm task rm

Delete tasks

#### Synopsis

Delete tasks by ID, or every task matching --all, --queue and/or --status (running tasks are stopped first). --files also deletes the partial and downloaded files.

A single ID uses delete-task; several IDs or a filter use delete-tasks and print one result per task.

```
dlm task rm [ID...] [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --all              delete every task
      --files            also delete the partial and downloaded files
      --queue string     delete the tasks of this queue ID
      --status strings   delete the tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
```

### dlm task segments

Show the segments of a task's download

#### Synopsis

Show the byte ranges a task downloads in parallel and how much of each is done, as last saved (about once a second while it runs).

```
dlm task segments ID [flags]
```

### dlm task set

Change a task

#### Synopsis

Change a task's name, directory, priority, labels or settings overrides.

--label replaces all labels. --set path=value and --unset path build a JSON merge patch of the task's settings: dotted paths, values parsed as JSON when valid (else a string); --unset makes the setting inherit again.

```
dlm task set ID [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm task set <id> --priority high --set speedLimit=1048576 --unset retry.maxAttempts
```

#### Options

```
      --dir string          new absolute download directory
      --label stringArray   label key=value (repeatable; replaces all labels)
      --name string         new file name
      --priority string     new priority: low, normal or high
      --set stringArray     set a setting override path=value (repeatable)
      --unset stringArray   remove a setting override (repeatable)
```

### dlm task set-url

Replace a task's link

#### Synopsis

Replace the link of a task, for example when it expired. The new link is probed and checked against what was downloaded so far (size, strong ETag, file name): on a match the download resumes where it stopped; on a mismatch --on-mismatch (default: the task's refresh.onMismatch) decides: restart discards the partial data, fail rejects the link. Running tasks must be paused first.

```
dlm task set-url ID URL [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm task set-url 01J… 'https://cdn.example.com/f.zip?token=fresh' --referrer https://example.com/
```

#### Options

```
      --header stringArray   request header Name=Value (repeatable)
      --on-mismatch string   when the link serves different content: restart or fail (default: the task's refresh.onMismatch)
      --page-url string      web page the link was found on
      --referrer string      Referer to send
      --user-agent string    user agent to send
```

### dlm task settings

Show a task's effective settings and where each value comes from

#### Synopsis

Show the task's effective settings (Defaults ⊕ Global ⊕ Queue ⊕ Task) with the level each value comes from (default, global, queue, task).

```
dlm task settings ID [flags]
```

### dlm task torrent

Show the swarm of a torrent task

#### Synopsis

Show the state, trackers, peers, bytes shared and share ratio of a torrent task: live while it runs, otherwise what its last run saved.

```
dlm task torrent ID [flags]
```

### dlm task update-tasks

Change several tasks at once

#### Synopsis

Set the priority, add or remove labels, patch the settings overrides and/or move each chosen task. Only the given fields change. Chooses tasks by ID, or every task matching --all, --queue and/or --status. Prints one result per task; exits 1 if any failed.

```
dlm task update-tasks [ID...] [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --all                        act on every task
      --label stringArray          label to add or change, KEY=VALUE (repeatable)
      --priority string            new priority: low, normal or high
      --queue string               act on the tasks of this queue ID
      --remove-label stringArray   label key to remove (repeatable)
      --settings string            JSON merge patch of the task settings overrides (null unsets a field)
      --status strings             act on the tasks in this status (repeatable or comma-separated)
      --to string                  also move the tasks to this queue ID
```


## dlm tls

Set up TLS for a daemon other machines connect to

### dlm tls init

Create a self-signed certificate and print its fingerprint

#### Synopsis

Create a self-signed certificate and key (cert.pem and key.pem in the config directory, the key readable by you only) for a daemon that other machines connect to, and print the fingerprint clients pin. Name the hosts and addresses clients use with --host. --apply also writes server.tls_cert and server.tls_key into the config file; the daemon reads them when it starts. To accept remote clients also set server.allow_remote and a listen address (see 'dlm config set').

```
dlm tls init [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm tls init --host nas.local --host 192.168.1.10 --apply
  dlm config set server.allow_remote true && dlm config set server.address 0.0.0.0:17171
```

#### Options

```
      --apply              also set server.tls_cert and server.tls_key in the config file
      --days int           how many days the certificate is valid (default 825)
      --dir string         where to write the files (default: the config directory)
      --force              replace an existing certificate and key
      --host stringArray   a host name or IP address clients connect to (repeatable); localhost is always included
```


## dlm token

Manage the API token

```
dlm token [flags]
```

### dlm token add

Create a named token

#### Synopsis

Create a named token for a dashboard, a script or another device and print its secret once. --scope read makes it read-only (it can read everything except cookie exports and the token list, and change nothing).

```
dlm token add NAME [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm auth token add dashboard --scope read
```

#### Options

```
      --scope string   admin (everything) or read (read-only) (default "admin")
```

### dlm token list

List the named tokens

```
dlm token list [flags]
```

### dlm token rm

Revoke a named token

```
dlm token rm ID [flags]
```

### dlm token rotate

Replace the primary token

#### Synopsis

Generate a new primary token, write it to the daemon's token file and stop accepting the old one at once. The new token is printed so a remote client can switch to it; clients on this machine read the file.

```
dlm token rotate [flags]
```

### dlm token show

Show the API token file (and, with --reveal, the token)

#### Synopsis

Show where the daemon's API token is stored. Use --reveal to print the token itself, e.g. to configure the browser extension. The token is created by `dlm serve`, never by this command.

```
dlm token show [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --reveal   also print the token (keep it secret)
```


## dlm version

Print the CLI and daemon versions

#### Synopsis

Print the CLI version and, if the daemon is reachable, its version. An unreachable daemon is not an error.

```
dlm version [flags]
```


## dlm watch

Stream live events from the daemon

#### Synopsis

Print events (task progress and status changes, queue and settings updates) as they happen.

Table output prints one line per event (TIME TYPE TASK QUEUE SUMMARY); json prints one JSON object per line (NDJSON); yaml prints one document per event. The stream reconnects automatically and resumes after the last received event. When events may have been missed (daemon restart, slow reader) a notice is printed to stderr. Stop with Ctrl-C.

```
dlm watch [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm watch
  dlm watch --type task.progress --type task.status --task <id>
  dlm watch -o json
```

#### Options

```
      --queue string   only show events of this queue ID
      --task string    only show events of this task ID
      --type strings   only show events of this type (repeatable or comma-separated), e.g. task.progress
```


## dlm webhook

Manage the webhooks that receive events

#### Synopsis

A webhook receives a JSON POST for each event it subscribes to (task.status, queue.completed, ...). With a secret every body is signed: the X-DLM-Signature header is sha256= and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body.

```
dlm webhook [flags]
```

### dlm webhook add

Create a webhook

```
dlm webhook add URL [flags]
```

#### Examples

```
  dlm webhook add https://example.com/hook --event task.status --event queue.completed --secret s3cret
```

#### Options

```
      --disabled            create the webhook switched off
      --event stringArray   event type to deliver (repeatable, required)
      --secret string       secret that signs the deliveries
```

### dlm webhook deliveries

Show a webhook's recent deliveries

#### Synopsis

Show the last attempts to send an event to the webhook since the daemon started, newest first: the event, the attempt, the HTTP status the endpoint answered, how long it took and what went wrong.

```
dlm webhook deliveries ID [flags]
```

### dlm webhook get

Show a webhook

```
dlm webhook get ID [flags]
```

### dlm webhook list

List webhooks

```
dlm webhook list [flags]
```

### dlm webhook rm

Delete a webhook

```
dlm webhook rm ID [flags]
```

### dlm webhook set

Change a webhook

#### Synopsis

Change the given fields of a webhook. --event replaces the whole list; --secret '' removes the secret; --enabled=false switches the webhook off.

```
dlm webhook set ID [flags]
```

#### Options

```
      --enabled             switch the webhook on or off (default true)
      --event stringArray   new event list (repeatable; replaces the old list)
      --secret string       new signing secret (empty removes it)
      --url string          new endpoint
```

### dlm webhook test

Send a test event to a webhook

```
dlm webhook test ID [flags]
```
